summary: Count subarrays (via prefix/suffix removal) by product modulo k, for k <= 5.
mainInsight: Let cnt[r] be the number of subarrays ending at the previous index with product % k == r. For a new value a, the new counts are new[(r * a) % k] += cnt[r] for every r, plus the single-element subarray new[a % k] += 1. Add new into the global result. This is O(n * k).
canonicalApproach: DP over remainders of subarrays ending at i

approaches.name: Brute force products
approaches.summary: Compute every subarray product mod k.

promptVariants: What does dp[i][r] represent for Find X Value of Array I?
options: The number of subarrays ending at i whose product modulo k is r
The product of the first i elements modulo k
The longest subarray ending at i with remainder r

cards.answer: The number of subarrays ending at i whose product modulo k is r
cards.explanation: Extend each subarray ending at i - 1 by nums[i]: remainder r becomes (r * nums[i]) % k.

promptVariants: Why is the state small and why can it be rolled?
What is added for the new single-element subarray?
cards.answer: k is at most 5, so there are at most 5 remainder buckets per index, and dp[i] depends only on dp[i - 1]. A new subarray starting and ending at i contributes one to bucket nums[i] % k. Summing dp over all i gives the final result array.
keyPoints: Depends only on the previous row

cards.explanation: For each element update k remainder buckets.

promptVariants: What is the result for nums = [2, 2, 1] and k = 2?
How many subarrays have an even product?
options: [5, 1]: five subarrays have an even product, one is odd
[1, 5]: one subarray is even, five are odd
[6, 0]: every subarray has an even product
[3, 3]: the six subarrays split evenly by parity
cards.answer: [5, 1]: five subarrays have an even product, one is odd
cards.explanation: Six subarrays exist. Only [1] has an odd product; every other subarray contains a 2, so its product is even: result[0] = 5, result[1] = 1.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[1, 5]: one subarray is even, five are o: The counts are reversed: most subarrays contain a 2 and are even.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[6, 0]: every subarray has an even produ: The single subarray [1] has product 1, which is odd.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[3, 3]: the six subarrays split evenly b: Containing a 2 makes a product even, so the split is not even.
